articles.description:
Lately, there’s a growing debate over whether AI will completely replace Robotic Process Automation (RPA). Some predict RPA’s imminent demise. But is this prediction realistic?
Here’s how we see it at Maybe:
Automation today comes in two main flavors:
Traditional RPA: Handles programmable, repetitive tasks. It’s predictable, stable, and efficiency-focused, like a factory assembly line.
AI Agent: Manages vague but describable goals. It’s flexible and adaptive—more like a personal assistant.
In short, RPA optimizes known tasks, while Agents handle unknown situations.
Technical feasibility shouldn’t overshadow cost:
RPA has a high initial setup cost but minimal ongoing expenses. After the upfront investment, it runs nearly for free.
Agents, however, require continuous interaction with Large L…
articles.title: Will AI Replace RPA? The Real Limits of Automation

articles.description:
Hey everyone 
We're a team of indie developers exploring tools for the Solana ecosystem.
SolCat - a lightweight app that helps you launch and manage SPL tokens directly through your Phantom wallet. 
Whether you're launching a meme token, experimenting with SPL tools, or building something more serious, SolCat helps you:
Whether you're launching a meme token, experimenting with SPL tools, or building something more serious, SolCat helps you:
Mint new tokens (SPL-compliant)
Revoke minting authority
Revoke freeze authority
Make metadata immutable
View token info and mint additional supply (if allowed)
Do it all through Phantom
There are many tools out there, but most are either too technical, too clunky, or require CLI/Web3 knowledge.

We wanted to create something:
Easy to use
Visually clean
Focused on security (with authority revoking and immutability as key features)
Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind + Phantom Adapter
Backend: Render + PostgreSQL (only for token record storage)
Blockchain: Solana (using @solana/web3.js and Metaplex SDK)
SolCat is live at: https://solcat.fun
If you're into Solana, Phantom, or building tools for creators and communities — we’d love your thoughts.

Feel free to drop suggestions, bug reports, or feature ideas.
Telegram: https://t.me/solcat_fun
articles.title: Launch Your Solana Token in Seconds — Introducing SolCat.FUN

articles.author: IBM Developer
articles.description:
This tutorial was originally published on IBM Developer.
Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how developers build applications, but they face a fundamental limitation: they operate in isolation from the data and tools that make applications truly useful. Whether it's accessing your company's database, reading files from your filesystem, or connecting to APIs, LLMs need a standardized way to interact with external systems.
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) addresses these limitations by providing a standardization layer for AI agents to be context-aware while integrating with the data and tools. Learn more about what MCP is, its client-server architecture components, and its real-world benefits in this “What is MCP?” article or in the MCP docs.
The following figure shows the typical MCP architecture, with MCP hosts, MCP clients, MCP servers, and your own data and tools.

In this comprehensive tutorial, we'll explore MCP and learn how to build a production-ready integration with IBM watsonx.ai, demonstrating how to create AI applications that can seamlessly connect to enterprise data and services.
Continue reading on IBM Developer to learn how to build context-aware AI applications using MCP with Granite models...
articles.title: Build context-aware AI apps using MCP
